subject: Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter

messages.author: 681145121914a526
messages.subject: Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
Dear Stan List,

I am relatively new to Stan, and I'd like to implement the following model:

i=1...n
Y[i,1] ~ poisson(lam[i,1])
Y[i,2] ~ poisson(lam[i,2])
lam[,] = exp(mu[,] + b[,])
b[i,1:2] ~ multi_normal(c(0,0), Sigma[1:2,1:2])
Sigma[1,1] <- sig1*sig1
Sigma[2,2] <- sig2*sig2
Sigma[1,2] <- sig1*sig2*tau
Sigma[2,1] <- Sigma[1,2]

Y is observed, sig1, sig2, mu are known, and tau is the unknown correlation parameter.

This is the R code to simulate the data:

library(MASS)
set.seed(1234)
n <- 100
beta1 <- c(1, -1)
beta2 <- c(0.5, 0.5)
sigma1 <- 0.5
sigma2 <- 0.8
tau12 <- 0.5
x <- runif(n)
X <- model.matrix(~x)
mu1 <- drop(X %*% beta1)
mu2 <- drop(X %*% beta2)
Sig <- diag(c(sigma1, sigma2)^2)
Sig[2,1] <- Sig[1,2] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau12
b <- mvrnorm(n, c(0,0), Sig)
Y1 <- rpois(n, exp(mu1 + b[,1]))
Y2 <- rpois(n, exp(mu2 + b[,2]))

dat <- list(n = n, Y=cbind(Y1,Y2), mu=cbind(mu1,mu2),
    sigma1=sigma1, sigma2=sigma2)

I tried to adapt pieces from the Stan manual and birats example, with no success so far. Here is the best I could come up with:

data {
    int<lower=0> n;
    int Y[n,2];
    row_vector[n] mu;
    real<lower=0> sigma1;
    real<lower=0> sigma2;
}
parameters {
    real<lower=-1,upper=1> tau;
    row_vector[n] loglam;
}
transformed parameters {
    cov_matrix[2] Sigma; 
    Sigma[1,1] <- sigma1*sigma1; 
    Sigma[2,2] <- sigma2*sigma2;
    Sigma[1,2] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau;
    Sigma[2,1] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau; 
} 
model {
    for (i in 1:n) {
        loglam[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma);
        Y[i] ~ poisson(exp(loglam[i]));
    }
}

but I get this error message:

TRANSLATING MODEL 'model' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name = model_name,  : 
  failed to parse Stan model 'model' with error message:
EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=22, column=9

        loglam[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma);
        ^-- here

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
    arg 0 type=real
    arg 1 type=real
    arg 2 type=matrix
available function signatures for multi_normal_log:
0.  multi_normal_log(vector, vector, matrix) : real
unknown distribution=multi_normal
Parser expecting: "}"

Any help would be much appreciated!

Thanks,

Peter Solymos

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
What you want is

model {
loglam ~ multi_normal(mu,Sigma);
Y ~ poisson(exp(loglam));
}

You may also need to define Y, mu and loglam as column vectors instead
of row vectors.

Cheers,
Marcus

array.

entire text of the error message?

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
Ok, my apologies, I didn't look closely enough at your model. You
actually need to define loglam and mu differently. One way to do it
is to use the following definitions:

matrix[2,n] loglam;

matrix[2,n] mu;

and with model block:

model {
for (i in 1:n) {

col(loglam,i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i),Sigma);
Y[i] ~ poisson(exp(col(loglam,i)));
}
}

Where the col() function extracts a column of the matrix.

Hopefully that helps, and sorry for the confusion.

Cheers,
Marcus

parts:
I'd also suggest replacing

Y[i] ~ poission(exp(...))

with

Y[i] ~ poisson_log(...);

It should be faster and more arithmetically stable.

The name _log is for the transform, and exp() is the inverse
transform.

More after the include.

...

>>>>> I tried to adapt pieces from the Stan manual and birats example, with no
>>>>> success so far. Here is the best I could come up with:

...
>>>>> parameters {
...
>>>>> row_vector[n] loglam;
...
>>>>> model {
...
>>>>> loglam[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma);

>>>>> but I get this error message:
>>>>>
>>>>> TRANSLATING MODEL 'model' FROM Stan CODE TO C++ CODE NOW.
>>>>> Error in stanc(file = file, model_code = model_code, model_name =
>>>>> model_name, :
>>>>> failed to parse Stan model 'model' with error message:
>>>>> EXPECTATION FAILURE LOCATION: file=input; line=22, column=9
>>>>>
>>>>> loglam[i] ~ multi_normal(mu[i], Sigma);
>>>>> ^-- here
>>>>>
>>>>> DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
>>>>> no matches for function name="multi_normal_log"
>>>>> arg 0 type=real
>>>>> arg 1 type=real
>>>>> arg 2 type=matrix
>>>>> available function signatures for multi_normal_log:
>>>>> 0. multi_normal_log(vector, vector, matrix) : real
>>>>> unknown distribution=multi_normal
>>>>> Parser expecting: "}"

loglam is an n-vector, so loglam[i] is a scalar. multi_normal
expects a vector.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
Hmmm, ok, there is a bug in Stan here, as anything that parses should
compile OK. That issue aside, you should be able to work around it as
follows:

model {
for (i in 1:n) {
col(loglam,i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i),Sigma);

Y1[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[i,1]);
Y2[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[i,2]);
}
}

The line with the uniform prior on tau is also not needed.

Cheers,
Marcus

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts: Thanks Marcus, that did the trick, but note I had to swap indices in loglam:

model {
for (i in 1:n) {
col(loglam,i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i),Sigma);

Y1[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[1,i]);
Y2[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[2,i]);
}
tau ~ uniform(-1, 1);
}

Now adaptation complains about Sigma not being positive definite, but
as far as I read on the list, this can be quite safely ignored:

"
Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis
rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue
(and please ignore that what comes next might say 'error'): Invalid
value of Sigma: Error in function validate transformed params d: Sigma
is not positive definite. Sigma(0,0) is 0.25.
If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a
problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be
drawn from the posterior.
"

Thanks for your help!

Peter

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
As the message indicates, this is only an issue if you see a lot of
them and the sampler isn't able to move. If you want to get rid of
this you can tweak the bounds on tau to avoid a nearly singular Sigma.
Specifically,

real<lower=(-1 + 1e-8),upper=(1 - 1e-8)> tau;

So tau can never quite get to 1 or -1.

Cheers,
Marcus

> }

> }

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
Of course!
I used
real<lower=-0.99,upper=0.99> tau;
which solved the issue.

Cheers,

Peter


On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 12:48 PM, Marcus Brubaker

<marcus.a...@gmail.com> wrote:
> As the message indicates, this is only an issue if you see a lot of
> them and the sampler isn't able to move. If you want to get rid of
> this you can tweak the bounds on tau to avoid a nearly singular Sigma.
> Specifically,
>
> real<lower=(-1 + 1e-8),upper=(1 - 1e-8)> tau;
>
> So tau can never quite get to 1 or -1.
>
> Cheers,
> Marcus
>
>
>
> On Tue, May 7, 2013 at 2:41 PM, Peter Solymos <sol...@ualberta.ca> wrote:
>> Thanks Marcus, that did the trick, but note I had to swap indices in loglam:
>>
>> model {
>> for (i in 1:n) {
>> col(loglam,i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i),Sigma);
>> Y1[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[1,i]);
>> Y2[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[2,i]);
>> }
>> tau ~ uniform(-1, 1);
>> }
>>
>> Now adaptation complains about Sigma not being positive definite, but
>> as far as I read on the list, this can be quite safely ignored:
>>
>> "
>> Informational Message: The parameter state is about to be Metropolis
>> rejected due to the following underlying, non-fatal (really) issue

>> is not positive definite. Sigma(0,0) is 0.25.
>> If the problem persists across multiple draws, you might have a
>> problem with an initial state or a gradient somewhere.
>> If the problem does not persist, the resulting samples will still be
>> drawn from the posterior.
>> "
>>
>> Thanks for your help!
>>
>> Peter
>>
>>
>>

>>> model {
>>> for (i in 1:n) {

>>> }
>>> }
>>>

parts:
If there's more to that warning message and you can include
it, we might be able to help diagnose what's wrong with the
configuration. (Though Ben's been known to guess without
any more than what you just said.)

You could try compiling the model through the command line
interface to see if the C++ can be set up properly.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Bivariate Normal model with unknown correlation parameter
parts:
Thanks Ben,
It's all good now. I post the current version below that works without
any errors/warnings/notes.
Cheers,
Peter

--

library(MASS)
set.seed(1234)
n <- 100
beta1 <- c(1, -1)
beta2 <- c(0.5, 0.5)
sigma1 <- 0.5
sigma2 <- 0.8
tau12 <- 0.5
x <- runif(n)
X <- model.matrix(~x)
mu1 <- drop(X %*% beta1)
mu2 <- drop(X %*% beta2)
Sig <- diag(c(sigma1, sigma2)^2)
Sig[2,1] <- Sig[1,2] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau12
ee <- mvrnorm(n, c(0,0), Sig)
Y1 <- rpois(n, exp(mu1 + ee[,1]))
Y2 <- rpois(n, exp(mu2 + ee[,2]))

joint_PLn <- '
data {
int<lower=0> n;
int<lower=0> Y1[n];
int<lower=0> Y2[n];
matrix[2,n] mu;
real<lower=0> sigma1;
real<lower=0> sigma2;
}
parameters {
real<lower=-0.99,upper=0.99> tau;

matrix[2,n] loglam;
}
transformed parameters {
cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
Sigma[1,1] <- sigma1*sigma1;
Sigma[2,2] <- sigma2*sigma2;
Sigma[1,2] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau;
Sigma[2,1] <- sigma1*sigma2*tau;
}
model {
for (i in 1:n) {
col(loglam,i) ~ multi_normal(col(mu,i),Sigma);
Y1[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[1,i]);
Y2[i] ~ poisson_log(loglam[2,i]);

}
tau ~ uniform(-1, 1);
}
'
dat <- list(n = n, mu=rbind(mu1,mu2), Y1=Y1, Y2=Y2,

sigma1=sigma1, sigma2=sigma2)

f <- stan(model_code=joint_PLn, data=dat)
